rules.surface_condition: cuts where the token immediately BEFORE the marker is a numeral/date
rules.blamed_rule: Left or right stretch that ends or begins with a lexical token translators typically render reliably will tend to raise the measured value. Examples of such surface forms: numerals and formatted numbers (e.g., "1,200", "2050"), explicit dates, percentages, currency figures, and short fixed named phrases (e.g., organization names, place names). (Prediction to test: cuts adjacent to numerals/dates often score high.)
rules.proposed_rule: Scoring Rules: do NOT give the usual top-tier boost to cuts adjacent to NUM tokens. Instead, push such positions into a mid band unless additional reliable anchors appear immediately after the marker. Target band for left_last NUM: 20–70 (use lower half when the left-side NUM sits in a prepositional/quantifier context).

rules.surface_condition: cuts where the token immediately AFTER the marker is the coordinator 'or'
rules.blamed_rule: Cuts before or after subordinators or coordinators can measure well when the segment to the left or right is itself translated reliably (e.g., if the left already ends in a named entity or numeral). Example surface words: "and", "but", "however", "when", "after", "since", "while", "which", "that", "who". Do not assume these always help; the testable prediction is only that presence of reliable lexical material on one side increases measured score.
rules.proposed_rule: Scoring Rules: lower the score for cuts whose right_first token is 'or' (target band 0–65). 'Or' commonly starts an immediate continuation/alternative that makes the right stretch fragmentary; only restore a high score if the token after 'or' is itself a strong anchor (NUM or a fixed name).

rules.surface_condition: cuts where the token immediately AFTER the marker begins a capitalized named-entity token (common org/place tokens observed here: 'tsunami','minae')
rules.blamed_rule: Left or right stretch that ends or begins with a lexical token translators typically render reliably will tend to raise the measured value. Examples of such surface forms: numerals and formatted numbers (e.g., "1,200", "2050"), explicit dates, percentages, currency figures, and short fixed named phrases (e.g., organization names, place names). (Prediction to test: cuts adjacent to numerals/dates often score high.)
rules.proposed_rule: Scoring Rules: raise the score for cuts whose right_first is an uppercase named-entity token (raise into the mid–high band). That is, when the segment AFTER the marker starts a likely organization/place/person token, prefer the cut (target band 60–95).

tie_fix: Ties are produced when multiple surface-based heuristics map different markers to the same canonical boost (e.g. many NUM/NAME cases get the same top boost); break ties deterministically by adding a tiny position-based offset (plus index) so equal-boost tokens are ordered consistently.
summary: The model systematically over-weights raw numerals and coordinator boundaries: cuts adjacent to NUMs are often scored too high even when the left segment is a prepositional/quantifier fragment, and cuts before 'or' are sometimes boosted because the left side looks lexical. It also under-weights some cuts that start an obvious named entity on the right. Tightening the numeral/name boosts (downgrading lone NUM-adjacent cuts), lowering cuts that lead into 'or', and explicitly raising cuts that open a named-entity on the right should improve overlap with the measured labels.
